Tarnobrzeg Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tarnobrzeg, Poland

Not demolished. This is the older of Tarnobrzeg's two Jewish cemeteries, likely established at the town's founding. In the 1840s, Rabbi Eliezer Horowitz (died 1860), progenitor of the Hasidic Dzików dynasty active in the city until WWI, settled in Tarnobrzeg. By 1890, Jews made up about 81 percent of the town's population. The cemetery closed before 1860, when a new one was established; in 1940, the Germans destroyed it, and the land was later used as a trading square before public buildings were constructed there.
